timeline.title: Saxon traces
timeline.description: The original church is thought to have been a small Saxon nave and chancel. Traces of early work remain and may date to around 950.

timeline.title: A church in Domesday
timeline.description: The Domesday Book entry for Mickleham records a church and two acres of meadow.

timeline.title: Norman work
timeline.description: Much of the present church dates to the Norman period, around 1180, including the chancel arch, lancet windows and font.

timeline.title: The Norbury Chapel
timeline.description: The side chapel, now called the Norbury Chapel, dates from around 1300. Its memorials include the Wyddowsoun tomb and brasses.

timeline.title: Restoration and change
timeline.description: The church underwent significant alterations: nave arches and piers were replaced in 1823, with further changes during the nineteenth century and the dismantling of the north aisle in 1891.

timeline.title: The bells
timeline.description: Four of the larger bells completing the peal of six were given in memory of Sir James Lawrence in 1913.

timeline.title: A living parish
timeline.description: St Michael and All Angels continues as a place of worship and community life for Mickleham and Westhumble.
